key_insight: Revisiting MgHCu3 shows that while its crystal and electronic structure are stable, its phonons and predicted superconducting Tc are highly sensitive to computational settings, bringing the original 42 K claim into question.
engineering_relevance: This work highlights that high-temperature superconductivity predictions for hydrides and perovskites must be validated across multiple functionals and k-point/phonon grids before they are used as design targets.
method: Recomputed crystal and electronic structure using PBEsol and PBE.
Evaluated lattice dynamics, phonon dispersion, and electron-phonon coupling under different k-point meshes and Gaussian broadenings.
Compared superconducting Tc predictions across numerical settings to test robustness.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports Tc values spanning roughly 10 to 31 K depending on Gaussian broadening, with phonon-related properties strongly dependent on grid density and functional choice.
watch_item: Predicted superconducting properties may be numerically fragile, so results should not be treated as reliable without cross-functional checks and experimental benchmarking.
